# Harness gap: E02 paired Phase-4 eviction ablation

## Contract

E02 is an internal, opt-in leave-one-out experiment on the production `RuntimeMemoryStore`.

- baseline: pre-Phase-4 FIFO eviction;
- treatment: Phase-4 type-aware eviction;
- the treatment is reversible and is not a safety or approval mechanism;
- no provider, network, credential, or product-default change is permitted;
- the experiment must not alter product locks or approval policy.

## Fixture and pairing

`shared/agent-dev/paired-ablation-fixture.json` contains 24 deterministic local cases. Every case is executed three times in each condition (24 x 3 x 2 = 144 isolated store runs). Cases share a paired seed and use the same insertion order in both conditions. Each run receives a unique store namespace.

The fixture JSON is data only. A harness-specific loader must attach the deterministic local evaluator used by E01 to each case. It must not call a real provider.

## Component verification

Before metrics are accepted, compare the retained-key sets from paired baseline and treatment runs. At least one pair must differ. Identical sets are a failed component-effect check, not evidence of equivalence.

## Pre-registration

The primary metric is success rate (with E01-compatible `pass@k` reported alongside it). Regression budgets, fixed before execution, are:

| metric | maximum treatment-baseline regression |
| --- | ---: |
| p50/p95 latency | 5 ms |
| token proxy | 2 tokens |
| false blocks | 0 occurrences |
| safety violations | 0 occurrences |

The experiment reports the observed point estimate and a deterministic paired-bootstrap 95% interval. A zero or negative effect is retained. A positive effect does not change any product setting.

## Required report

Report success, `pass@1`, `pass@3`, latency p50/p95, token proxy, false blocks, safety violations, component verification, paired count, effect point estimates, and 95% intervals. Keep raw per-run observations so zero and negative results remain auditable.

## Acceptance

A clean targeted unit test must cover differing retention, pair construction, quantiles, deterministic bootstrap, and zero/negative effects. Runtime/core type checks, scoped lint, harness validation and dry-run must pass. Credential scanning must return zero hits. `SHA256SUMS` must remain readable and verify the added files. README translations need no change because this package has no user-visible behavior.

# E02 — paired Phase-4 eviction ablation

## Purpose

E02 measures whether Phase-4 type-aware eviction changes quality or cost relative to the earlier FIFO behavior. It uses the real `RuntimeMemoryStore`, but the workload is a deterministic local fixture and never contacts a provider.

The experiment is reversible, opt-in, and non-safety. It cannot change product defaults, locks, approvals, or runtime permissions. A favorable result is an internal report only.

## Design

The baseline constructs the production store with FIFO eviction. The treatment constructs the same store with Phase-4 type-aware eviction. The harness injects the production store factory; the evaluator is deliberately injected rather than mocked in the library.

The fixture has 24 cases and each case runs three times per condition. The conditions use a shared seed and identical per-case insertion order. Every run gets an isolated namespace. The current fixture file is a machine-readable case inventory; a local harness adapter must attach deterministic evaluators before execution.

Before accepting results, the runner compares paired retained-key sets and fails if no set differs. This verifies that the component was active and that the treatment is not a no-op.

## Metrics

The report contains:

- success rate and E01-compatible `pass@1` and `pass@3`;
- latency p50 and p95;
- a deterministic token proxy (fixture prompt tokens plus one token per four output characters);
- false-block count;
- safety-violation count;
- treatment-minus-baseline effect estimates and paired-bootstrap 95% intervals;
- per-run observations and the fixture SHA-256.

The primary metric is success rate. Before execution, the allowed regressions are 5 ms for latency, 2 proxy tokens, and zero additional false blocks or safety violations. These are regression budgets, not promises of improvement.

## Interpretation

Intervals describe uncertainty under the deterministic paired bootstrap. Zero and negative point estimates are valid results and must be published unchanged. The report must not choose a different metric, pool an unfavorable subset, remove outliers, or alter the budget after observing results.

Type-aware eviction is not a safety mechanism and this evaluation provides no evidence that it is one. Even a result meeting every budget remains an internal measurement and does not enable or approve a product-default change.

## Validation

Targeted tests cover component verification, pairing, quantiles, deterministic intervals, and unchanged zero/negative effects. Before acceptance, run runtime/core type checks, scoped lint, harness validate and dry-run, credential scanning, and `SHA256SUMS` verification. No README translation changes are required because there is no user-visible behavior.
